chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Lester Young's language and politeness
summary: Lester used code words instead of swearing, and wore crepe-soled shoes.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Uh-huh. When you -- after you got to New York it was that you and Lester Young became friends wasn't it? I mean good friends.
Did you work with him in New York?
No. We palmed around a lot. And he was the -- (laughter) -- you know Jo Jones had a language all his own (unintelligible), never know what he was talking about. Now
Lester would never swear. If he wanted to say M. F., he would say "Orrin Tucker" and if he wanted to say K. M. A., he'd say "Whispering Grass" (Laughter).
Can you think of any other ones?

(Laughter). One night comming in Lin-ton's Playhouse. I don't know what caused this but someone hit Lester in the eye. (Laughter). Lester say "wow!" A Sunday A Rainy!" (Laughter). Meaning the person hit him while he wasn't looking, you know. (Laughter). But I never heard an obscenity come out of this man's mouth. Everyone thought that he was sort of epheminate you know, because he was so polite.
I'd say you let him hear you say that, you know. And then they'd say his brother is too, Lee is too, isn't he? I'd say no, they just walk like that, you know.
Well Lee didn't walk like that did he?
Well Lester did have kind of a mincing walk but I've never known Lee walked that way.
Well he doesn't walk now like I remember Lester walking.
No, no. Well there was a reason for Lester walking the way he walked. Because he always worked in creped sole, canvas topped shoes.
